CHIEF COMPLAINT
Right finger pain.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Sharon Brooks is a 48-year-old female presenting with right index finger pain. Patient reports injury occurred while skiing over the weekend (4 days ago). She was attempting moguls when her strap caught on her finger, causing it to hyperextend and bend backwards. Patient has tried ice application and ibuprofen, but pain persists. Movement worsens the pain.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Not discussed.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Constipation (recent). Appendectomy at age 18.

MEDICATIONS
Miralax for constipation. Ibuprofen (over-the-counter) for finger pain.

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient participates in skiing.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Right index finger examined. Tenderness noted over the distal phalanx (tip of finger) and over the distal interphalangeal joint. No tenderness over proximal interphalangeal joint or metacarpophalangeal joint. Pain with flexion. Patient able to bend and extend finger. Patient able to touch thumb with affected finger. No other abnormalities noted.

RESULTS
X-rays of right index finger: Normal, no fractures, normal alignment.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Right hand index finger contusion on tip of finger, no fracture. Plan: Aluminum foam splint for immobilization. Motrin 600 mg every 6 hours for approximately one week. Patient to call and return if symptoms do not improve.
